headline: GM gives OnStar an AI makeover with new assistant and app
summary: The automaker is integrating a new AI assistant into its OnStar service, starting with the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq EV. This move aims to transform OnStar into a connected intelligence platform.
details: General Motors is revamping its 30-year-old OnStar connected car service by introducing a personal AI assistant. This new OnStar AI Assistant will debut in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq EV and will be rolled out to more GM vehicles subsequently.

The company also announced a new OnStar mobile app set for a 2027 launch, which will replace existing OnStar Guardian and brand-specific apps. This initiative is part of GM's strategy to build a significant subscription business.

Unlike previous updates, this reboot centers on agentic AI, aiming to make OnStar a proactive support mechanism rather than just a call center. GM has been progressively integrating AI, using Google Cloud's Dialogflow and planning for Gemini integration in 2026.

The OnStar AI Assistant is an in-house development designed to offer an interactive and personalized experience for drivers and passengers. It will leverage vehicle cameras for live views and safety recordings, with features like automatic event capture triggered by sensed events.

Users will be able to control vehicle functions such as climate settings and query specific features using voice commands. This AI integration is crucial for GM to keep pace with technological advancements in the automotive industry.

GM has faced criticism and fines for data sharing in the past. The company assures that customers will control data sharing, and recordings will be time-limited and encrypted, with GM and OnStar unable to access Connected Camera recordings.
